<description>
{
 "summary": "Validates Tor onion service IDs and private keys returned by the Tor control port and read from disk before using or caching them. It requires service IDs to resolve to valid Tor v3 addresses, verifies private keys against the Ed25519 v3 format with 64-byte payloads, and ensures replies without service IDs do not adopt keys or reuse state.",
 "problem": "Tor reply parsing unescapes quoted strings, allowing a rogue or compromised Tor control port to return a `PrivateKey` containing CRLF line breaks or spaces. Because the node inserts cached keys unquoted into `ADD_ONION` commands on reconnect, CRLF enables Tor control command injection (such as `SIGNAL SHUTDOWN`) and spaces inject command arguments. In addition, previous logic retained state across replies and attempted to advertise and cache keys for invalid service IDs.",
 "evidence": [
  "PR description: 'Tor reply parsing unescapes quoted values, so a control endpoint can return a value containing a line break or space. On reconnect, the node inserts that value unquoted into an ADD_ONION command. CRLF frames the remainder as a separate command, while a space adds further arguments.'",
  "Functional tests added in test/functional/feature_torcontrol.py explicitly demonstrate injecting 'SIGNAL SHUTDOWN' via CRLF and 'Flags=Detach' via spaces in returned and cached private keys."
 ],

<category name="p2p" title="P2P">
## Covers

Everything between this node and other nodes: connection management and
peer selection, address management, the message protocol and its
transport (including the encrypted v2 transport), block and transaction
relay including compact blocks, headers sync, transaction request and
orphan handling, network-level DoS protections, and the Tor, I2P, and
CJDNS integrations. The P2P and Private Broadcast labels are a strong
prior.

Not p2p: what the node does with a block or transaction once received
(validation, mempool); RPCs that merely report peer state (rpc).

## What matters here

Resistance to attack first: eclipse and partition resistance, DoS
resistance in message handling and resource accounting, and privacy of
transaction origin. Then relay correctness and liveness: blocks and
transactions propagate reliably and quickly, and nothing gets stuck.
Then interoperability with the rest of the network and with new
protocol features (BIPs) that other software depends on. Then bandwidth
and resource use, which node operators feel. Then connectivity across
network types and platforms.

Protocol changes with a specification and other implementations
waiting rank higher than local optimizations. Refactors count when they
retire a known hazard in message handling.
